frequency_question: How often do central banks deploy unexpected incremental reserve ratio mandates within a short operational window when excess liquidity signals appear?
membership_rule: Includes any formal secondary or incremental reserve ratio announcement by major emerging market central banks targeting systemic liquidity management. Excludes standard annual adjustments to baseline reserve requirements.
window: Any multi-month operational window within the post-2010 monetary policy era.

cases.name: PBoC Reserve Requirement Ratio hike for liquidity management (Dec 2010)
Bank of Russia additional reserve requirements (2014)
Central Bank of Brazil compulsory deposit requirement tightening (2021)

provenance_note: 4 cases named, 10 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.5x)
coverage_note: 4 named primary instances; estimated roughly 10 comparable systemic liquidity surplus episodes globally in the past decade where ad-hoc reserve ratios were deployed.
known_gaps: Varying definitions of secondary reserve requirements across different central bank jurisdictions.
skeleton: Central bank liquidity absorption cycles across major emerging economies where surplus shocks occur, decomposed into systemic liquidity surplus episodes leading to ad-hoc instrument deployment.
multiplier: 4 observed hits out of 10 major systemic liquidity surplus episodes where secondary reserve ratios were considered.
validity_reason: Monetary policy frameworks regarding liquidity management instruments remain stable over multi-year horizons unless major structural reforms occur.
